records.title: Perturbation-efficient Zeroth-order Optimization for Hardware-friendly On-device Training
records.reason: PeZO reduces random-perturbation generation resources for zeroth-order on-device model training using an efficient perturbation scheme; evaluation reports lower hardware resource/power costs for training. It is explicitly training-time optimization and does not address inference/serving. The link to an FPGA inference paper is insufficient for a direct lineage connection.

records.title: NSFlow: An End-to-End FPGA Framework with Scalable Dataflow Architecture for Neuro-Symbolic AI
records.reason: NSFlow maps neuro-symbolic workloads to a scalable FPGA dataflow architecture and evaluates end-to-end framework performance on neuro-symbolic AI tasks. Its hardware flow is not evaluated on transformer/LLM inference and does not provide an LLM-specific operator or serving result. FPGA is shared with linked works, but relation remains broad architectural adjacency.

records.title: DRViT: A dynamic redundancy-aware vision transformer accelerator via algorithm and architecture co-design on FPGA
records.reason: DRViT co-designs token merging/pruning and INT8 with an FPGA ViT accelerator; reported evaluation runs ViT-Tiny on ImageNet and compares FPGA resources/performance. Limitations note hardware/model differences require adaptation. The contribution is specifically vision-transformer acceleration, with no language model or LLM inference experiment; FTRANS connection is hardware-family-level only.

records.title: LongSafety: Enhance Safety for Long-Context LLMs
records.reason: LongSafety proposes safety evaluation/mitigation for long-context LLM behavior and evaluates safety under long inputs. The measured goal is reducing unsafe responses, not reducing compute, memory, latency, or serving overhead. Its cited long-context lineage overlap is topical only, without a technical efficiency connection.

records.title: Resource-Efficient Personal Large Language Models Fine-Tuning With Collaborative Edge Computing
records.reason: This work partitions personal LLM fine-tuning across collaborative edge devices to reduce fine-tuning resource burden, with experiments on edge collaboration and model quality/communication. Its objective is training, not generation/inference serving, and it does not establish inference-time memory/latency improvement. Linked 4-bit inference work is only adjacent.
